Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:10:1.hebrew: הא - דקתני אבל לא ישקם במועד, היינו ר"א בן יעקב, דאמר אבל לא ישקה את כל השדה כולה. והא דתני בין במועד בין בשביעית, היינו חכמים, דמתירין להשקות אפי' כל השדה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:10:1.english: This - [the baraita] that teaches, "but one may not water them on [the intermediate days of] the Festival," is [the opinion of] Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov, who says, "but one may not water the entire field." And [the baraita] that teaches, "both on [the intermediate days of] the Festival and during the Sabbatical Year," is [the opinion of] the Sages, who permit watering even the entire field.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:11:1.english: So that they will sprout during the Sabbatical Year - But one may not water [it] during the Sabbatical Year so that they will sprout during the Sabbatical Year.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:12:1.english: One may trap moles [ishut] - in an orchard on [the intermediate days of] the Festival, because they cause damage in it.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:12:2.english: In his [usual] manner - For he does not need to alter [his method] in trapping.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:12:3.hebrew: ובשביעית - אע"ג דמתקן השדה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:12:3.english: And during the Sabbatical Year - Even though he improves the field.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:12:4.english: In an orchard - He traps in his [usual] manner, because it is a substantial loss.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:12:5.hebrew: ובשדה לבן שלא כדרכו - ואינו יכול לצוד כדרכו בשדה לבן, משום דלא מפסיד כולי האי בשדה לבן:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:12:5.english: And in a field of grain, not in his [usual] manner - And he may not trap [them] in his [usual] manner in a field of grain, because he does not suffer that much of a loss in a field of grain.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:13:1.english: And one may seal a breach - That if part of it [the wall] collapsed, one may go back and repair it on the Festival.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:13:2.hebrew: ובשביעית בונה כדרכו - מתחילה, אע"ג דמיחזי דעביד נטירותא לפירי:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:13:2.english: And during the Sabbatical Year one may build in his [usual] manner - From the outset, even though it appears that he is making a safeguard for the produce.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:14:1.english: A creature that has no eyes - And [it] digs in the ground.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:14:2.english: What is the verse - [indicating] that an ishut [is] a creature that has no eyes.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:14:3.hebrew: דכתיב כמו שבלול תמס יהלך - שבלול, שקורין לימצו"ן. תמס יהלך — כלומר כשיוצא חוץ מנרתיקו, רירות נופלות ממנו עד שהוא נימוח ומת. תמס, כמו ונמס:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:14:3.english: As it is written, "As a shablul that melts and goes" - Shablul is [the creature] that they call limaçon [a snail, in Old French]. "Melts and goes" — that is to say, when it emerges outside of its shell, slime falls from it until it dissolves and dies. Temes [is] like venamas [melted].

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:14:4.hebrew: נפל אשת בל חזו שמש - כלומר, כך אישות נופלות פתאום לארץ ומתים, דלא חזו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:14:4.english: The fall [nefel] of a mole [eshet] that has not seen the sun - That is to say, so [too] do moles [ishut] fall suddenly to the ground and die, because they do not see.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:15:1.english: And they strangle each other - Because they smell the soil and do not recognize that soil.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:16:1.hebrew: והוא דקאי בתרי עברי נהרא - דכיון דאיכא הפסק מים בין הני תרתי חורי נמלים, אין מכירים הני בעפר דהני:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:16:1.english: And this [applies] when they are on two sides of a river - For since there is an interruption of water between these two ant holes, these [ants] do not recognize the soil of those [other ants].

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:16:3.english: A plank bridge (gamla) - [Meaning] that [the river] has no [actual] bridge, only a single plank.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:16:4.hebrew: ומצרא - עדיין קטן מגמלא, אין יכול להלך עליו אלא כשקושרים חבל אחד משני עברי הנהר בשתי יתידות, ואוחזין בו והולכין על אותו גשר צר. אבל אי איכא חד מהן, מכירין הני בחורי דהני:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:16:4.english: And a mitzra - [It is] even smaller than a gamla [plank bridge]; one cannot walk upon it unless they tie a single rope across the two sides of the river to two stakes, and they hold onto it and walk upon that narrow bridge. But if there is [even] one of them, these [ants] recognize the holes of those [ants].

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:1:1.hebrew: רובע - הקב, אחד מכ"ד בסאה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:1:1.english: A quarter - [of] a kav, [which is] one twenty-fourth of a se'ah.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:1:2.hebrew: הכי גרס ימעט - שאם זרע רובע הקב, ימעטנו ויעקרנו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:1:2.english: This is the reading: [one must] reduce - For if one sowed a quarter-kav, one must reduce it and uproot it.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:2:1.english: But isn't it taught [that they pronounce] the entire field [ownerless] - Yet you say one must reduce [it]?

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:3:1.hebrew: שמנכשין שדותיהן - שלוחי ב"ד משלהן, דכשנוטלין הכלאים, מאליו מתנכש:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:3:1.english: That they weed their fields - The agents of the court [do so] at their own [expense]; for when they take the diverse kinds, [the field] is weeded of itself.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:5:1.hebrew: מושכין המים מאילן לאילן - דהוי כשדה בית השלחין, דפסידא יתירא איכא, אבל לא ישקה את השדה כולה, שדה בית הבעל:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:5:1.english: One may draw water from tree to tree - For it is like an irrigated field [beit hashelachin], where there is a substantial loss; however, he may not water the entire field, [which is] a rain-watered field [beit haba'al].

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:5:2.english: Plants that were not watered prior to the Festival - [Meaning] that they were not accustomed to drink [i.e., be watered] regularly prior to the Festival.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:5:3.hebrew: לא ישקם במועד - דהואיל ולא משקה להו תדיר לפני המועד, לא הוי ליה פסידא אי לא משקה להו במועד:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:5:3.english: One may not water them on the Festival - For since he does not water them regularly prior to the Festival, he does not incur a loss if he does not water them on the Festival.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:5:4.hebrew: וחכמים מתירים בזה ובזה - להשקות את כל השדה כולה, ולהשקות במועד זרעים שלא שתו לפני המועד. והאי חכמים היינו ר"מ, דאמר לעיל (מועד קטן דף ב.): משקין ממנו אפילו שדה בית הבעל:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:5:4.english: And the Sages permit in this [case] and in that [case] - to water the entire field, and to water on the Festival seeds that were not watered before the Festival. And these "Sages" are Rabbi Meir, who said above (Moed Katan 2a): "One may water from it even a rain-watered field."

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:6:1.hebrew: אמר רב יהודה - הא דאמר ר"א: "אבל לא ישקה את השדה כולה" — אבל אם היתה שדה מטוננת — לחה ויבשה — מותר להשקותה, אע"ג דהוה שדה בית הבעל; דכיון דהויא לחה עד השתא, אי לא משקה לה הוי פסידא יתירא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:6:1.english: Rav Yehuda said - [Regarding] that which Rabbi Eliezer [ben Ya'akov] said: "However, he may not water the entire field" — if, however, the field was metunenet — [meaning] damp, and it dried out — it is permitted to water it, even though it is a rain-watered field [beit haba'al]; for since it was damp until now, if he does not water it, there is excessive loss.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:7:1.english: A dry field - [One that has] always [been] dry, such that there is no need to water it.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:7:2.english: In this and in that - In [the case of] a dry field and in [the case of] seeds that had not drunk [i.e., had not been watered] before the Festival.

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:8:2.hebrew: שרי לתרבוצי - לזלף עליה מים, אע"ג דליכא פסידא. לתרבוצי — להשקות, לשון "אין מכבדין ואין מרביצין", היינו השקאה פורתא כדי שיצאו הירקות, וכדמפרש באידך ברייתא לקמיה; ומשקין — היינו השקאה גמורה של בית השלחין:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:8:2.english: One is permitted to sprinkle [letarbutzei] - To sprinkle water upon it, even though there is no loss. Letarbutzei [means] to water, [from] the expression "one may not sweep and one may not sprinkle [marbitzin]" — that is, a light watering so that the vegetables will sprout, and as [the Gemara] explains in the other baraita further on; whereas "watering" [mashkin] means a full watering of an irrigated field [beit hashelachin].

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:8:3.hebrew: אפלא לשוויי חרפא - דליכא פסידא, ואפ"ה שרי להשקותה כך ולהשביחה. ה"נ בגינה מרביצין:
Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:8:3.english: A late [crop] to make [it] an early [crop] - For there is no loss, and even so it is permitted to water it thus and improve it. Here too, in a garden, we sprinkle [water].

Rashi on Moed Katan 6b:9:1.english: A field of grain - A rain-watered field.

Tosafot on Moed Katan 6b:12:1.hebrew: צדין את האישות במועד ובשביעי' - תימה: מאי קמ"ל בשביעית? והלא אין זו עבודת קרקע? ורבי יהודה, מאי טעמא דאסר כדרכו? וי"ל דודאי צריך למיסקל אבנים מתוך שדהו כשמפנה האישות, ותנן פ"ג דשביעית: "המסקל שדהו נוטל העליונות ומניח התחתונות הנוגעות בארץ, וכן גרגיר של צרורות וכו'". אישות — מפורש בירושלמי: חולדה:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 6b:12:1.english: "One may trap the ishut on a Festival and during the Sabbatical Year" - It is astonishing: What does [the Mishnah] teach us regarding the Sabbatical Year? Surely this is not work of the land! And Rabbi Yehuda — what is the reason that he forbids [trapping] in his usual manner? And one can say that he certainly needs to clear stones from his field when he removes the ishut, and we learned in a Mishnah in Chapter 3 of Sheviit: "One who clears stones from his field takes the upper ones and leaves the lower ones that touch the ground, and similarly a heap of pebbles, etc." Ishut — it is explained in the Yerushalmi [that it is] a chuldah [a weasel or mole].

Tosafot on Moed Katan 6b:7:1.hebrew: ואין משקין שדה גריד - פי': בית הבעל, לפי שהוא רגיל להיות יבש. וגריד בדל"ת, וכן פירש בערוך; [ובתוס'] הרב — ברי"ש, כמו "חמרא מיגרר גריר" (פסחים דף קז:):
Tosafot on Moed Katan 6b:7:1.english: And one may not water a dry [garid] field - Explanation: [This refers to] a rain-watered field [beit haba'al], because it is accustomed to being dry. And garid [is spelled] with a dalet, and so [too] did the Arukh explain; [and in Tosafot] HaRav [it is spelled] with a reish [i.e., garir], like "chamra migrar garir" [wine draws the appetite] (Pesachim 107b).

Tosafot on Moed Katan 6b:7:2.hebrew: וחכמים מתירין בזה ובזה - והני תרי פלוגתא דבהך ברייתא, היינו כעין פלוגתא במתניתין; ות"ק דהכא הוא ר"א בן יעקב:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 6b:7:2.english: "But the Rabbis permit [watering] in this [case] and in that [case]" - And these two disputes in this baraita are like the dispute in the Mishnah; and the first Tanna here is Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov.

Tosafot on Moed Katan 6b:8:1.hebrew: שרי לתרבוצי - וקשה, הא קיימא לן משנת ר"א קב ונקי! ועוד הקשה בתוספות דרבינא גופיה, דאמר לעיל (מועד קטן דף ד.): מדלין ירקות כדי לאוכלן, אבל לייפותן אסור — אלמא הרווחא אסור. ותירץ דתרביצא אינה כ"א השקאה פורתא. ולפ"ז נראה דה"פ: דהאי תרביצא שרי לתרבוצי אפילו לראב"י, דכי היכי דשרו רבנן אפלא לשוויי חרפא, גם לראב"י יתיר ג"כ השקאה פורתא; או שמא סבר כר"א בהשקאה ופליג בהרבצה. וי"מ דפלוגתא דשדה גריד לאו היינו פלוגתא דמתני' דמיירי בה ראב"י וחכמים, ופליגי באפלא לשוויי חרפא: ת"ק חשיב ליה הרווחא ואסור, ורבנן סברי דלאו היינו הרווחא, דיש אוהב יותר אפלא ויהיו נגמרים יותר ומבושלים בטוב. ור"ח פי': אמר רבינא שמע מינה האי תרביצא — פי' שדה שאין זרוע עדיין שכבר השקוהו קודם, מותר להשקותו במועד לזורעו אחר המועד, דסבר לה כראב"י דאמר זרעים ששתו לפני המועד, וקסבר תרביצא הוי כמו זרעים ששתו לפני המועד, דהיינו שם תרביצא שהרביצוהו קודם המועד. ומקשינן עלה: שדה גריד אסור משום דאי משקי ליה האידנא יבכיר קודם אבל לא פסיד, תרביצא נמי אי משקה האידנא קדים ובכיר ולא פסיד! וזה השיטה הולכת דסבירא לן כראב"י, כך פירש ר"ח:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 6b:8:1.english: One is permitted to sprinkle - And this is difficult, for we hold [that] the teaching of Rabbi Eliezer [ben Yaakov] is "a kav and clean" [i.e., concise and authoritative, and he prohibits watering a dry field]! Furthermore, it was asked in Tosafot regarding Ravina himself, who said above (Moed Katan 4a): "One may thin out vegetables in order to eat them, but to beautify them is prohibited" — thus we see that [acting merely for] profit is prohibited! And he answered that tarbitza is nothing other than a slight watering. According to this, it seems that this is the meaning: that this tarbitza is permitted to be sprinkled even according to Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, for just as the Rabbis permit [turning] a late crop into an early crop, so too according to Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov he [Ravina] would also permit a slight watering; or perhaps [Ravina] holds like Rabbi Eliezer [ben Yaakov] regarding [full] watering and disagrees [with him] regarding sprinkling. And some explain that the dispute regarding a dry field is not the [same] dispute as that of the Mishnah in which Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov and the Sages are dealing, and they disagree about [turning] a late crop into an early crop: the first Tanna considers it profit and [therefore] it is prohibited, whereas the Rabbis hold that this is not [considered] profit, because there is one who prefers a late crop so that they will be more fully grown and well ripened. And Rabbenu Chananel explained: "Ravina said: Learn from here [that] this tarbitza" — meaning a field that is not yet sown, which they already watered beforehand, it is permitted to water it on the Festival [i.e., Chol HaMoed] in order to sow it after the Festival, for [Ravina] holds like Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov who said "seeds that drank before the Festival" [may be watered], and [Ravina] holds that tarbitza is like seeds that drank before the Festival, for that is [the meaning of] the term tarbitza: that they sprinkled it before the Festival. And we raise a difficulty against it: A dry field is prohibited because if one waters it now, it will ripen earlier, but it does not suffer a loss; [so too with] tarbitza, if one waters [it] now, it will be early and ripen [earlier], and it does not suffer a loss! And this approach proceeds [on the premise] that we hold like Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov. Thus explained Rabbenu Chananel.

Tosafot on Moed Katan 6b:9:1.hebrew: מרביצין שדה לבן בשביעית - לגבי שביעית פי' הקונטרס השקאה פורתא, ונראה שחזר בו ממה שפירש במשנה "משקין בית השלחין במועד" — ולגבי שביעית שרי אפילו בית הבעל. ואני פירשתי במשנה דשביעית נמי לא שרי אלא בבית השלחין, כדפי' בקונטרס כאן. אבל ק"ל: שמא הכא איירי בהשקאה גמורה, דפליגי לגבי מועד ראב"י ורבנן, ופלוגתייהו הוי בהשקאה מרובה! ואדרבה, נראה לי דמיירי בהשקאה גמורה, אלא לגבי שלחין שצריך השקאה נקט "משקין", וגבי בית הבעל קרוי "הרבצה". לכן נראה יותר פי' הקונטרס שבמשנה. ולפי' דהכא צ"ל דהשקאה גמורה אסורה בבית הבעל, והרבצה מועטת שרי בשביעית; ובמועד אסור אפילו הרבצה מועטת לר"א בן יעקב, ולרבנן שרי אפ' השקאה גמורה:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 6b:9:1.english: One may sprinkle a white field during the Sabbatical Year - Regarding the Sabbatical Year, the Kunteres [Rashi] explained [that "sprinkling" means] a small amount of watering. It appears that he retracted what he explained on the Mishnah, "One may water a beit hashelachin [an irrigated field] on the Festival" — [namely, that] regarding the Sabbatical Year, even a beit haba'al [a rain-watered field] is permitted [for full watering]. And I explained on the Mishnah that [during] the Sabbatical Year as well, [full watering] is only permitted in a beit hashelachin, as the Kunteres explained here. However, I have a difficulty: Perhaps here [the baraita] is dealing with complete watering, since Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov and the Rabbis disagree regarding the Festival, and their dispute is regarding abundant watering! On the contrary, it appears to me that [the baraita] is dealing with complete watering, except that with respect to shelachin, which requires watering, it uses the term "watering" [mashkin], whereas with respect to beit haba'al, it is called "sprinkling" [harbatzah]. Therefore, the explanation of the Kunteres on the Mishnah appears more [plausible]. And according to [his] explanation here, one must say that complete watering is forbidden in a beit haba'al [during the Sabbatical Year], and slight sprinkling is permitted during the Sabbatical Year; while on the Festival, even slight sprinkling is forbidden according to Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov, whereas according to the Rabbis, even complete watering is permitted.
